headline: Your CleanCloud waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing laundromats, dry cleaners, alterations, and shoe-repair shops into the right CleanCloud POS, pickup-and-delivery, multi-store, or starter offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Ricard Pryce.
productSummary: CleanCloud (cleancloud.com / cleancloudapp.com) is cloud POS + pickup/delivery + customer-app SaaS for laundromats, dry cleaners, shoe repair, and alterations. Homepage: Launch, Manage and Scale Your Laundry from One Platform; all-in-one for managing and scaling a laundromat, dry cleaning, shoe repair and alterations business; Loved by / Trusted by 5,000+ of the Best Laundromats and Dry Cleaners. Product surfaces: Point of Sale (easy UI, detailing, payments, digital waivers, automated SMS/Email/Push/WhatsApp, first-order identifier); Pickup and Delivery (customer app, driver app, route planning, photos/signatures/chat, DoorDash and Uber, repeat orders); Marketing (website builder, Google Business Profile Book Now, email/SMS/push, automated flows, review requests on Google/Yelp/Facebook/Nextdoor); Workflows (wash-and-fold tracking, MetalProgetti/QuickSort auto and assisted assembly, lockers, barcode tagging, washer/dryer payment integrations, multi-store plant). Named quotes: Daniel Logan, Columbia Pike Laundry — scale from one store to a full pickup & delivery business; Charles Measley, Fluff & Fold Laundry — over 30,000 pick up and delivery orders in 21 months; WashBar Laundries — 4 stores and growing; Aaron Cardelino, Wasfo — grow to different locations throughout Florida or across the United States. Features page: from 1-1000 stores; LaundryCard, FasCard, Laundroworks, Tangerpay & SpyderWash integrations; Speed Queen and Huebsch; DoorDash and Uber; route optimizer; branded iOS/Android customer apps; QuickBooks and Xero. Pricing (cleancloudapp.com/pricing): Lite (500 orders/mo), Pro (2,000 + pickup & delivery, Uber & DoorDash, route optimization, driver app, subscriptions, assisted assembly, multi-store), Grow (3,000 + auto assembly, automated marketing, automated review promotion, automated invoicing, API), Grow+ (10,000 + branded iOS/Android customer app, dedicated AM); pay monthly or yearly (save up to 20%); 14-day free trial. Grow+ claim: see 122%* more orders with your own custom app — *Based on CleanCloud customer data. Blog (starting-a-laundry-business-a-pricing-strategy): plans starting at just $99 a month. Homepage CTA also frames current state as Pen and Paper. Dollar amounts for Lite/Pro/Grow/Grow+ are not printed on the public pricing table — do not invent them in copy.
coreInsight: Ricard already sells one laundry operating system so shops stop running tickets, routes, and customer comms on pen-and-paper, a Windows dry-clean POS, or a laundromat-only stack that does not cover garment care plus pickup-and-delivery in one login. The one list is local laundry services only: Google Maps laundromats, dry cleaners, alterations, and shoe-repair shops in the English-speaking markets CleanCloud already sells into — not restaurants, not generic retail POS. The one routing signal is maps_ops_state: how the shop already shows up on Maps, because a Places scrape already returns a competitor POS named in reviews or on the site, pickup-and-delivery attributes on the listing, same-brand location count, or none of those, in one pull. Category (laundromat vs dry cleaner vs alterations) is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how the shop already shows up on Google Maps
sections.takeaway: A Places scrape already names a competitor POS in reviews or on the website, pickup-and-delivery attributes on the listing, same-brand location count, or none of those. That maps_ops_state is stronger than a title guess, and it is cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM laundry shop
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Named competitor POS in reviews or on-site goes first, then listings that already advertise pickup and delivery, then same-brand multi-site operators, then every remaining Maps laundromat, dry cleaner, alterations, or shoe-repair shop.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each Maps ops state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor POS shops get a Switch Brief. Pickup-and-delivery listings get a Route & App Brief. Multi-site operators get a Multi-Store Plant Brief. The rest get the Pen-and-Paper POS Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the POS, productise pickup, roll up stores, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM local laundry services — laundromats, dry cleaners, alterations, shoe repair — aimed at owners and operators. Shop type is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the Maps state already on the listing
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor POS, the pickup-and-delivery attribute, or the extra locations, poke the ticket/route/multi-store pain that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor-POS route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay Cents, SPOT, Sera, Fabricare, or a peer and still leak cloud POS, routes, or a customer app. Prove reply density, then roll pickup-and-delivery listings, multi-site operators, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Google Maps (Places) is the TAM Ricard already sells into: laundromats, dry cleaners, alterations, and shoe-repair shops in English-speaking markets CleanCloud ships to (US, UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore named on the Xero app listing as markets — treat as geo gate, not a headcount). TAM account count is not published on cleancloud.com; treat size as unknown and keep each launch tier ≥~1,500 contacts.

The same Places pull returns maps_ops_state: competitor POS named in reviews or on the shop site, pickup-and-delivery / wash-and-fold booking attributes, and same-brand location count — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product. LaundryCard, FasCard, Speed Queen, and Alliance are CleanCloud integrations, not switch targets.

The ladder maps to live CleanCloud positioning: all-in-one vs a named POS; Pro pickup-and-delivery (customer app, driver app, route optimizer, DoorDash/Uber) on cleancloudapp.com/pickup-and-delivery; multi-store plant and 1–1000 stores on the features page; homepage Pen and Paper as the remaining-TAM starter state; 14-day trial and Lite-from-$99 (blog) as the soft offer.

Shop type (laundromat vs dry cleaner vs alterations) and owner title are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the listing is routed, never the TAM spine alone.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor detected (Cents, SPOT / Spot Business Systems, Sera, Fabricare / Enlite, Geelus, DRYCLEAN PRO, Wintux / SMRT, Comca, or another named laundry/dry-clean POS in Google reviews or on the shop website)
routingRules.why: They already pay for laundry POS. Strongest intent for CleanCloud's all-in-one pitch: cloud POS + pickup/delivery + customer app + marketing in one platform, Trusted by 5,000+ shops, 14-day trial. Integrations (LaundryCard, FasCard, Speed Queen) are the migration path, not the enemy.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND no Tier-1 competitor AND pickup_delivery_signal present (GBP attributes or listing copy for pickup, delivery, wash-and-fold booking, or Book online)
routingRules.why: They already sell pickup and delivery on Maps, so the leak is routes, driver proof, and a customer app — not education about delivery. Maps to Pro: Pickup & Delivery, Uber & DoorDash, route optimization, driver app (cleancloudapp.com/pricing and /pickup-and-delivery). Charles Measley: over 30,000 pick up and delivery orders in 21 months.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND no Tier-1 competitor AND no Tier-2 pickup_delivery_signal AND location_count >= 2 (same-brand Places cluster)
routingRules.why: Two or more listings, still no named POS and no advertised P&D. Pain is split tickets and no plant view. Features page: from 1-1000 stores; multi-store plant, shared customer/product database, metrics across stores. Homepage: WashBar — 4 stores and growing; Wasfo — locations throughout Florida or the US.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (Maps laundromat, dry cleaner, alterations, or shoe repair). Homepage explicitly frames Pen and Paper as the starting state. Softest CTA: Lite POS, hosted website, 14-day trial, blog starting at $99/mo. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1

Pro adds Uber/DoorDash, route optimization, driver app, multi-store. Grow+ branded app: 122% more orders (CleanCloud customer data on pricing). 14-day trial. LaundryCard/FasCard/Speed Queen stay as integrations, not rip-and-replace hardware.

tiers.pain: Orders, payments, and ready-notifications still sit on paper tickets or a generic till, and there is no CleanCloud layer yet. Homepage frames this as Pen and Paper.

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam definition: Google Maps laundromats, dry cleaners, alterations, and shoe-repair shops in English-speaking markets CleanCloud sells into (US, UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore appear on the Xero app listing — use as a geo gate). Restaurants, retail, and non-laundry local businesses are out of this TAM.

Pull Places by category + city, then review/site scrape for competitor, GBP attributes for pickup_delivery_signal, and same-brand clustering for location_count. Suppress known CleanCloud customers when visible. Named homepage quotes are not a blanket exclude. Do not treat LaundryCard, FasCard, Speed Queen, Huebsch, or Alliance as competitor_POS.

Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear (target ~1 positive / 150-300). Do not launch a tier under ~1,500 contacts. Per-tier account counts and overall TAM size are flagged unknowns — not published on cleancloud.com. Do not invent shop-count or TAM numbers in copy.
Add Tier 2 pickup-and-delivery listings once Tier 1 copy is stable.
Add Tier 3 multi-site operators, then the catch-all for remaining in-TAM Maps shops.
Enrich emails via Apollo only after the listing is routed (GBP phone/email first).
A/B POS Switch Brief vs Columbia Pike / Fluff & Fold proof on Tier 1 before cloning angles downward. Optional chaos test: 5,000+ social proof vs 14-day trial / $99 start on the catch-all.
